facts.fact: A director at the Ministry of the Interior states that Rumonge is the 12th commune of Burundi whose civil status service is digitalised, and that the process will continue in other communes; no total of communes or offices is given.

The project launched at Rumonge on 19 July 2024 is for the digital registration of births and deaths at the commune's civil status service, at the commune seat and in its zones, so that each child born is registered directly, as FVS-Amade and the Ministry of the Interior state.

The local NGO FVS-Amade is to give Rumonge commune's civil status service computers, tablets, solar panels and routers and to train its agents, in a project lasting one year; participants at the launch doubted the commune could keep digital registration going without that support, and no domestic budget is named.
The communal administrator of Rumonge states that until this project births and deaths in the commune were registered by hand in registers.

systems.country_label: enregistrement numérique à l'Etat-civil / service d'Etat-civil digitalisé
systems.owner: commune civil status services under the Ministry of the Interior, Public Security and Community Development; at Rumonge equipped by the NGO FVS-Amade
systems.tiers: 12 communes as of July 2024, Rumonge the 12th; at Rumonge the commune seat and its zones

note: No `made` fact for the digital entry: the document says registration will take place at the commune seat and in the zones, with routers for connection, but does not say the record is held in a national register or stays in the office. The `paper` fact is the administrator's statement of what the project replaces at Rumonge. The ministry director calls digitalisation government policy but names no plan.
